title: Tomato and Onion Salad
subtitle: Ripe summer tomatoes with red onion, olive oil and fresh basil
excerpt: Thickly sliced ripe tomatoes with very thin red onion, dressed in olive oil and a little red wine vinegar, scattered with fresh basil. A salad that lives or dies by the quality of the tomatoes.
sourceNotes: Tomato and onion salad appears across Mediterranean and British summer cooking as a simple way of serving ripe tomatoes. The insalata di pomodori of southern Italy, the Turkish salata of tomatoes and onions, and the British summer tomato salad all follow the same basic formula: ripe tomatoes, raw onion, olive oil and herbs. The dish requires ripe tomatoes; nothing can compensate for using them underripe.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dress and leave for 15 minutes; the tomatoes release juice that enriches the dressing. Do not refrigerate.

content.text: Tomato and onion salad needs ripe tomatoes. Cold, hard supermarket tomatoes give a salad with no flavour. Ripe tomatoes sliced thick and left for 15 minutes after dressing are a different dish: the juice runs into the oil and forms a natural dressing. Do not use tomatoes straight from the fridge.

items.prepNote: ripe, at room temperature, cored and thickly sliced

content.text: Arrange the tomato slices on a large plate, overlapping slightly. Scatter over the thinly sliced red onion. Drizzle over {{olive-oil}} of olive oil and the red wine vinegar if using. Sprinkle with {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Scatter the torn basil over. Leave for 15 minutes before serving; the tomatoes will release juice that enriches the dressing. Do not refrigerate.

items.fix: Never refrigerate tomatoes: cold destroys the volatile compounds that produce flavour. Let them ripen at room temperature until they smell sweet. In winter, use cherry tomatoes or sun-dried tomatoes for a different but flavourful alternative.

items.symptom: Red onion is too sharp and raw-tasting
items.fix: Soak the sliced onion in cold water for 10 to 15 minutes, then drain and pat dry. This removes the harsh sulphurous edge without losing the crunch.

content.text: Tomato and onion salad appears in almost every Mediterranean cooking tradition in some form. In Britain it has been part of the summer salad repertoire since the 19th century, when garden tomatoes would appear from late July. It is one of the few salads that needs nothing from the store cupboard beyond salt, oil and vinegar, and nothing from the cook beyond patience for the tomatoes to come to room temperature.
